title: Chamberland–Meisters eigenvalue conjecture for injectivity
statement:
Let $F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a $C^1$ map. Suppose there exists an $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $F'(x)$,

$$
|\lambda|\geq\varepsilon.
$$

**Chamberland–Meisters conjecture.** Then $F$ is injective. This conjecture is presented as a sufficient condition for injectivity after the real Jacobian conjecture was disproved; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.03615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).
source_name: Wei Liu and Quan Xu, “A minimax principle to the injectivity of the Jacobian conjecture”, arXiv:1902.03615 (2019).
